input.quote: shall be furnished and maintained on terms and conditions which shall be no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier for transmission facilities of similar type and quantity transiting the location involved
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation burdening us. Searches for "most favoured/favored", "favourable/favorable", "no less" and non-discrimination language surface only two provisions, and both run in our favour: (i) Subparagraph 15.2 requires the transiting facilities to be furnished on terms "no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier", an MFN-style undertaking owed by the Terminal Parties (defined in (s) as China Telecom, CWHKTI, Chunghwa Telecom, KDD, Korea Telecom, NTT Com, PLDT, SingTel and Telekom Malaysia — Teleglobe USA Inc. is not among them), and (ii) Subparagraph 17.2 requires the Terminal Party's negotiated arrangements to be "reasonable and non-discriminatory". We are a beneficiary of both as a non-Terminal Party and Carrier, and we are nowhere obliged to extend to any other Party the best terms we grant to third parties. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation), so the fallback limits on product scope, 12-month duration and like-for-like carve-outs are not engaged, and no redline is warranted — the counterparty-granted MFN should be preserved.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
